summary.headline: Pine Labs FY26 revenue grew about 19% with adjusted EBITDA up to Rs.559 Crores in Q4; FY27 revenue guided to 21%-23.5%.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as delivering about 19% full-year revenue growth, roughly 500 bps EBITDA margin expansion, and full-year PAT of about Rs.113 Crores. Q4 operating cash flow was about Rs.676 Crores, but management said this should not be viewed in isolation, with full-year operating cash flow at about Rs.395 Crores. Q4 growth shortfall was attributed mainly to infrastructure deployment delays (about 2 lakh POS machines backlogged due to a chip shortage) and softness in Middle East and airline business. The company gave a hard FY27 revenue growth guidance of 21%-23.5%, and said Q1 FY27 would be at the lower end.

financial_highlights.change: H2 FY26 growth about 20%-21% per management
vs Rs.357 Crores in the year-ago quarter
About 50% growth per analyst question, not disputed
Run-rate capex about Rs.180-190 Crores after adjusting for older DCP payments

segments.name: Digital infrastructure and transactions
segments.commentary: Covers offline infrastructure (about 2 million touchpoints), flow/transaction services, and fintech infrastructure for banks and merchants. Management expects at least 2%-3% improvement in infrastructure growth versus earlier assumptions.

segments.name: Issuing and acquiring
segments.commentary: Now about 30% of revenue. Issuing growing in India and globally; employee benefits program to launch in the next few weeks to quarters; stablecoin-backed prepaid platform sales to start within a month.

segments.name: Online
segments.commentary: Online business grew about 60% YoY; all three large e-commerce and top three quick-commerce players use Pine Labs as a platform. Shopflo acquisition is product-led and not material to growth; guidance excludes inorganic contribution.

segments.name: International (IAP)
segments.commentary: International growing about 44% per management; Philippines has five clients including GCash; POS services launched in Singapore; two head-to-head wins against global payment majors.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth hard guidance of 21%-23.5% YoY (headline revenue, not net revenue); guidance excludes inorganic boosters.
Q1 FY27 expected at the lower end of the range; growth to improve in Q2, Q3 and Q4.
Management did not give specific EBITDA guidance for FY27 but expects significant adjusted EBITDA improvement; reiterated 55% incremental contribution-to-EBITDA conversion as a floor.
Contribution margin expected to vary by 2%-3% due to business mix (employee benefits and new lines), with no underlying margin pressure per management.
Operating cash flow expected to improve significantly in FY27.
capex_capacity: Q4 capex of Rs.238 Crores included about Rs.160-170 Crores for DCPs and older payments; run-rate capex about Rs.180-190 Crores.
Chip shortage delayed POS deliveries; advances paid to suppliers sit in CWIP, and alternate suppliers were onboarded.
OMC (oil marketing company) rollout: about 50,000 of targeted 130,000 POS terminals deployed, roughly 50% of steady state by volume; about 50,000 pumps in the program.
Backlog of about 2 lakh POS machines in Q4 carried into Q1, now described as cleared with supply chain in place.
demand_pricing: Affordability (EMI/credit at point of purchase) penetration under 10% of market; non-electronics affordability is less than 5% of the book and growing; EV affordability traction emerging.
Activation ratio of POS machines for flow/transaction services improved to 30% from 21% a year earlier.
Unit economics in some segments improved about 7% in six months; sub-enterprise merchant (5-6 stores) infrastructure grew about 30% YoY.
Management reports competitors pulling back from OMC and low-ticket segments as uneconomic; pricing described as improving in some segments.
Working capital held in 14%-15% range; bill discounting/early settlement program ran Rs.202 Crores of early settlement cash inflows in the quarter per analyst.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 tracking to the 21%-23% guidance and will growth be consistent across quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident in the hard guidance; Q4 shortfall was about Rs.20-25 Crores from infrastructure deployment delays and Middle East softness. Q1 expected at the lower end of the range, improving from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Affordability take rate fell from about 35 bps to 30 bps and working capital cycle shortened; is this the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30 bps is a blended flow take rate affected by UPI and DCC mix; pure affordability take rates remain strong. Working capital held at 14%-15% beyond early settlement; bill discounting is an ongoing program, not one-time.

qa_highlights.question: Is there headroom to monetize GTV growth of about 50% when revenue grew 19%?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; monetization varies by segment (transaction- or value-based). Value-based revenue and data services are growing and recurring revenue is most of the mix.

qa_highlights.question: How many net new terminals will the OMC contract add and what additional services does it bring?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50,000 of 130,000 terminals deployed; OMC revenue includes forecourt integration, loyalty and IOT tenders. Indian Oil extra power loyalty contract is about Rs.60-65 Crores over five years, worth about 30-40 bps of growth uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split between affordability and VAS, and what drove the CM question?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split affordability and VAS. Contribution margin is net-revenue based (distribution is the only gross line); a 2%-3% variance is expected from mix as employee benefits launch.

risks_watch: Chip and component supply delays on POS deployment; Q1 FY27 deliveries and CWIP conversion.
Working capital and early-settlement reliance (Rs.202 Crores inflows in Q4) and whether take rates hold near 30 bps.
Affordability softness if consumer durable demand weakens; bank subvention pullbacks.
Geopolitical effects on Middle East and airline revenue and cross-border flows.
Accounting treatment and contribution margin for the employee benefits business launching in 45-60 days.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and cash flow, with clear hedging where management declined to give numbers (affordability split, contribution margin, EBITDA guidance). Management was defensive on Q4 growth shortfall and working capital questions, attributing them to supply and timing factors.
key_quotes: We think we will be able to grow at about 21% to 23.5% on a year -on-year basis as far as revenue is concerned.
I am going to be the first one to tell you that this Rs.676 Crores should not be looked at on a standalone basis.
Today for a bank and a retailer to replace or displace Pine Labs is a nine months effort.
Answer around crypto is a very clear no.
